jobs.description:
Streaming TV is no longer just a brand awareness channel. It’s becoming a core part of the performance marketing mix, alongside search and social. Vibe.co is building the platform that makes TV work like the rest of the acquisition stack: targeted, measurable, and optimized for results.

Vibe.co is an Audience First Streaming TV Advertising platform that gives marketers the tools to reach the right audiences, optimize campaigns in real time, and understand what’s actually driving business outcomes. With hyper-targeted segmentation, AI-powered recommendations, real-time optimization, and incrementality measurement, Vibe brings the precision and accountability of digital advertising to the biggest screen in the house.

Today, more than 12,000 brands use Vibe.co to reach 120 million+ households. And in August 2026, Vibe.co became a Walmart company, opening up a new chapter for the business and the industry. With Walmart’s first-party data and purchase signals now part of the Vibe platform, advertisers can connect TV advertising to real-world transactions and measure the impact of CTV with a level of precision previously associated with platforms like Google and Meta.

This is a unique moment to join Vibe. With Walmart’s scale, data, and reach behind us, we’re building the next generation of TV advertising and creating a more measurable, performance-driven future for the channel.

Your team

You will join the Supply team, which owns Vibe's inventory: the publishers we partner with, the deals we run, and the catalog of apps, channels and shows our advertisers care about.

Shows are the reason people turn on their TV. Advertisers don't just want impressions: they want to show up next to the right shows, live sports and premium channels. Supply brings that content to Vibe through direct publisher partnerships, curated deals and sponsorships. It makes it easy to find, understand and buy, through real-time bidding, or any technology the publisher uses.

Premium publishers care as much about which ads run on their shows as about who buys them, and great creatives are what earn us access.

The team brings together partnerships, operations, and product. You will work closely with the DSP team, which runs the bidding infrastructure, and the Performance team, which decides how to value each opportunity, as well as with publisher partners directly.

Your mission

As a Senior Software Engineer on Supply, you will build the systems that let Vibe grow, operate, and trust its inventory. You will turn publisher partnerships into live, healthy supply, and give the business and our partners the tools to manage it at scale.

What you will do

Publisher integrations

  • Build and improve publisher integrations end-to-end, from onboarding a new partner to supporting new ad formats and sponsorship offers.

  • Implement measurement requirements with publishers and the DSP team (e.g. UID2, publisher IDs) so the bidder sees richer inventory.

  • Own integration health: detect broken or degraded supply before it costs us spend.

Deals & catalog

  • Build the services behind deal setup, catalog management, and price configuration, in partnership with DSP on the deal API.

  • Automate the routine work of the Supply team (new deals, stale-supply cleanup, troubleshooting) so it scales with the number of partners, and with Vibe.

  • Enrich the catalog with content data (shows, genres, live events, channels) so advertisers can find what they are looking for, and even enjoy looking for it.

Supply tooling & publisher platform

  • Build real-time monitoring, alerting, and analytics on supply volume, quality, and spend.

  • Build publisher-facing features: reporting, insights, and self-serve catalog tools.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years of experience as a software engineer building and operating backend systems in production.

  • Strong programming skills (Go, Python and/or Rust), with real engineering discipline: testing, code review, CI/CD, maintainable design.

  • Hands-on with AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex or similar) in your day-to-day engineering workflow.

  • Experience integrating with external partners' systems and APIs, and owning those integrations when they break.

  • Comfortable owning services from code to production: cloud infrastructure (AWS or GCP), Kubernetes, and the observability to know your systems are healthy.

  • Product sense: you like talking to the people who use what you build, and you turn ambiguous business needs into concrete deliverables.

  • Excellent communication in English, with internal teams and with partners' technical contacts.

  • Pragmatism over purity: a bias toward shipping value.

Nice to have

  • Experience in AdTech or programmatic: OpenRTB, SSPs, PMP / PG deals, VAST.

  • Knowledge of the CTV ecosystem (publishers, apps, FAST channels).

  • Experience with identity solutions (UID2 or similar).

  • Experience building partner-facing or B2B dashboards and reporting.

Our Values

At Vibe, we run on three values: Impact, Ambition, and Urgency. We tie every goal to a real business outcome, think 10x rather than settling for good enough, and move daily rather than waiting for perfect conditions.

You’ll thrive here if you own outcomes without needing direction, default to action, and hold yourself to results, not effort.

This is a high-performance environment with high-performance rewards: you’ll work alongside people who push you, with real ownership over hard problems in a market that’s moving fast.

If that sounds like the best version of your career, we want to meet you.

What We Offer

The base pay range for this role in Paris is €90,000 – €125,000. We will support relocation to Paris for great candidates.

The base pay range for this role in New York is $140,000 – $200,000. We will support relocation to New York for great candidates.

At Vibe, we want you to build something, own something, and grow fast. Here’s how we back that up:

  • Variable pay — Based on real Vibe business goals.

  • Hybrid flexibility — We’re in the Heart of Paris and our team is in 3x a week!

  • Health insurance — Full coverage via Alan.

  • Meal vouchers — Via Swile.

  • Annual offsite — The whole team, once a year, somewhere worth the trip.

  • Tech Syncs — Engineering and Product meet in person at least quarterly, worldwide.

Our Interview Process

We respect your time. Here’s exactly what to expect, no surprises, no ghosting.

  1. Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes. We’ll share more context on the role and team, and learn more about your background and what you’re looking for.

  2. Hiring Manager Interview — 45 minutes. Meet with the person you’d work with directly and dive deeper into your experience, product background, and approach to the role.

  3. Technical Discussion — 90 minutes. A deeper conversation covering product thinking, measurement methodology, data reasoning, and a use case relevant to the role.

  4. Bar Raiser Interview — 30 minutes. Meet with a senior leader at Vibe for a final conversation and an opportunity to ask any remaining questions.

  5. Offer — We move quickly once we’ve made a decision. We don’t let good decisions sit.

jobs.title: Senior Revenue Operations Manager
jobs.description:
lemlist is the outbound platform for sales teams: find leads, run multichannel campaigns (email, LinkedIn, calls), personalize with AI and book meetings.

lempire also builds lemwarm (deliverability), Claap (AI call intelligence), Taplio and Tweet Hunter.

We're at +$60M ARR, growing ~50% year over year, profitable and 100% bootstrapped, with 180 people.

Your mission

lemlist and Claap sell through several motions at once: self-serve, sales-led, account management and partners. More than a quarter of our ARR sits in 1,200+ accounts managed by our Customer Success and Account Management teams. In 2027, these teams start working the same portfolio under a new customer segmentation, and expanding our existing accounts, including cross-selling Claap and our new products, is one of our biggest bets of the year.

As Senior Revenue Operations Manager (Customer Ops), your mission is to design how our revenue motions run, and own the systems and data behind them. In the short term, your focus is customer operations, from the moment Sales hands over an account to every renewal and expansion. Over time, the role can evolve toward Sales ops, Partnerships or other revenue topics, depending on your strengths, your interests and company priorities.

You'll join our Finance & Operations team, six people today, and report to Philippe, Head of Finance & Operations. Your main stakeholders are the leaders of Customer Experience, Account Management, Sales and Partnerships.

This is a hands-on role. You'll spend most of your time in HubSpot, our customer tools, automations and dashboards, building things people use every day. You also bring the business view: you know your numbers better than anyone, and you turn them into clear recommendations for the teams you work with.

Where you'll make an impact

Your first focus: customers

Give customer teams one view of every account. Bring product usage, billing and CRM data together, so every account tells the full story in one place. Own the build-or-buy decision on our customer platform, lead the rollout, and build with the Data team the dashboards that make CSMs' day-to-day easier and give leadership clear visibility on the customer base.

Build our risk detection engine. Turn usage, payment and engagement signals into early alerts across the whole portfolio, from our largest accounts with a dedicated CSM to the ones we manage at scale, so teams act on churn risk weeks before a renewal.

Make renewals and NRR predictable. With our VP CX and Account Management leaders, build the renewal and NRR forecast leadership can rely on, at least two quarters ahead, and know which accounts will grow, stay or churn.

Turn our customer base into expansion revenue. Give Account Managers and CSMs the signals and pipeline to upsell and cross-sell Claap and our new products, and track what it brings.

Also in your scope

Alongside customer ops, you'll contribute to the rest of our RevOps work:

  • Sales: make selling lemlist, Claap and new products simple for our reps, with lead routing, pipeline and performance tracking, and clear rules of engagement between Sales, Account Management and partners.

  • Partners: make partner deals easy to track, credit and pay, from PartnerStack to the CRM, so the Partnerships team can scale its programs in Europe and the US.

  • Systems: keep CRM and revenue data reliable as we add products, run commission plans people trust, and replace manual work with automations and AI agents.

What success looks like

Within your first 3 months

  • You've audited our customer motion and shared a 12-month plan with Philippe, our VP CX and Account Management leaders.

  • The customer platform decision is made, based on your recommendation.

  • A first version of the churn risk alerts is live for CSMs.

Within 12 months

  • CSMs and Account Managers work from one view of every account, with usage, billing and CRM data they trust.

  • Churn risks are flagged weeks ahead, and teams act on them before the renewal.

  • Leadership plans on your renewal and NRR forecast

  • You've turned the CRM into an expansion and pipeline generation tool, across lemlist and Claap.

  • Your work contributes to a measurable lift in net revenue retention (NRR) on the managed portfolio.

  • Sales and Partnerships see the difference too: clear rules of engagement, reliable routing, and partner deals credited and paid on time.

Who you are

  • 5+ years in RevOps or GTM Ops in B2B SaaS, ideally PLG + SLG.

  • You've owned customer operations for a portfolio at scale (health scores, churn risk, renewal forecasting), and led at least one big change: a tool rollout, a new coverage model or a new customer segmentation. Sales or partner ops experience is a plus.

  • Hands-on CRM admin experience (HubSpot)

  • Experience with a customer platform (Gainsight, ChurnZero, Planhat or similar) is a plus.

  • Business sense: you turn data into a recommendation and defend it with senior stakeholders.

  • You're used to working with VPs and the C-level, and you don't need a brief to start.

  • Builder mindset: you automate, use AI daily, document what you build and close what you start.

  • Fluent French and English.

If you read our values and thought "this is 100% me", you'll thrive in this role.

What is in it for you

  • A senior role with real ownership in a small team: you shape how a $60M+ ARR company sells and grows its customers.

  • You own the customer ops function

  • Direct work with VPs, the COO and the CEO.

  • AI by default: we already run AI agents on our CRM and internal tools, and we expect you to reach for AI first in everything you build.

  • Profitable, bootstrapped and growing 40+% a year: you build for growth without fundraising pressure.

  • Remote-friendly, async culture, with a Paris office.

Recruitment process

  1. Interview with Victoire (Lead TA).

  2. Interview with Oriane (COO).

  3. Business case (async) and live debrief with Philippe (Head of Finance & Operations) and Guillaume (VP Customer).

  4. Final interview with Charles (CEO).

  5. Reference checks and offer.

jobs.description:
lemlist is the outbound platform for sales teams: find leads, run multichannel campaigns (email, LinkedIn, calls), personalize with AI and book meetings.

We're at +$60M ARR, growing ~50% year over year, profitable and 100% bootstrapped, with 180 people.

lemlist is moving upmarket. We’re hiring a GTM Experience Manager to build our field marketing channel from scratch: bring in bigger deals and help our strategic customers stay and grow with us.

You’ll get the right people in the room and make it worth their time, with speakers they want to hear from, topics they care about and experiences they’ll tell others about. We want people talking about lemlist, and Sales walking away with real opportunities.

You’ll decide which conferences are worth investing in, what to build with partners and which events we should run ourselves. You’ll own the budget and make it happen, working closely with Marketing, Partnerships and Sales.

The scope is worldwide, with a focus on Europe and our Paris HQ as the home base for our own events.
It includes events for lemlist but also for claap, the sales intelligence platform we bought one year ago (same target audience).

What your impact will look like

Within 3 months, you’ll have:

  • Drafted our field strategy for lemlist: audience, objectives & how to reach them through events & strong sales/partners collaboration

  • Identify, negotiate & start action plan for 2 must-attend paid Events for lemlist

  • Design & organise 2 events with our most strategic partners and generate good pipeline out of it (that would make us breakeven if we have the usual ASP & CVR)

  • Built a clear operating model with Sales for pre-event outreach, rep selection, on-site activation and follow-up

  • Started creating one owned event format that can become recognizable lemlist franchise (eg. GTM monthly breakfasts…)

  • Organise at least one workshop for one of our strategic account/customer (at our or their HQ)

Within 12 months, you’ll have:

  • Generated 2M$ pipeline out of events, paid or owned - and are breakeven overall (total events OPEX spending < ARR signed and influenced)

  • Made lemlist events a must-be place for our ecosystem and audience

  • Run regular workshops for our top customers with CSMs, our Product leaders and/or our CEO, driving measurable adoption and upsell, and producing a steady flow of customer storiesz

  • Become the internal expert on the GTM event ecosystem (paid & partners): you know all the relevant events globally, who attends them, which ones are emerging and which ones are declining

  • Built a clear investment strategy across sponsored events & owned events with a strong point of view on where we spend and why

  • Build strong relationships with our key partners & some GTM communities, thanks to successful events

  • Built a measurement framework that lets us understand ROI: meetings, pipeline, revenue, brand impact, etc.

  • Built a repeatable playbook for selecting and activating the right Sales reps at each event so we maximise impact before, during and after

  • Bonus project: launch the lemlist swag store and build a rewards program to engage prospects, celebrate users and strengthen partner relationships.

What you’ll do concretely

You’ll manage two main types of events:

  • Sponsored events:

    • third-party conferences and trade shows.

    • You’ll build lemlist’s presence through booths, speaking opportunities and creative activations (eg. lemlist @ VivaTech)

    • …sometimes by creating our own event around a major industry moment.

  • lemlist events:

    • experiences organised by lemlist for prospects, customers or both.

    • Meetups at our HQ, the lemhouse in Avignon, executive dinners, IRL workshops in coffees or any venue of your choice.

    • Webinars with our team, partners a/o users, for our prospects & clients

    • You may run them independently or with some of our partners.
      → Recent examples: Event for a client at our HQ ; Hackathon with Clay and HubSpot.

Curate the right events and partners

  • Spot the difference between an outdated tradeshow that won’t attract our buyers anymore and the next place our audience will actually want to be (eg. recent AI / GTM trendy events)

  • For sponsored events, evaluate sponsorship opportunities based on audience quality, pipeline potential and brand impact. Assess audience & sponsor list (competition can be a good sign), ask feedback to operators that have been there.

  • Negotiate sponsorship packages to secure the best value, visibility and booth location. There is ALWAYS room to negotiate.

  • Proactively identify the right partners to build events with, and know when to push back on opportunities that are not worth our time.

  • Find and convince great speakers to join us for our events. Including customers, sales leaders, operators and partners.

  • Oversee the creation of agendas, talks, workshop programs and speaker materials, with support from the wider Marketing team.

  • Own every event from idea to execution, ensuring a smooth experience for attendees, speakers, partners and the lemlist team.

  • Own a €300K annual budget covering field marketing activities.

jobs.title: Director, Customer Success
jobs.description:
About Prudentia Sciences

Prudentia Sciences is the scientific intelligence layer powering life sciences dealmaking. We bring together expert-developed scientific diligence frameworks, AI reasoning trained on drug development, and a unified evidence base to accelerate investment in breakthrough therapies. As a trusted third party operating between buyer and seller, we help build conviction through every stage of the deal, faster. We replace fragmented workflows with a single system that surfaces what matters earlier.

 

Backed by GV (Google Ventures), McKesson, Iaso Ventures, Virtue, and SignalFire - and built by people who have sat on every side of the table in life sciences dealmaking - we're on a mission to bring expert scientific judgment to every deal decision, at AI scale.

 

The Opportunity

We're looking for a Director of Customer Success to manage and scale a portfolio of strategic biopharma accounts. You'll own commercial outcomes for Top 25 biopharma customers, driving platform adoption, retention, and expansion to build a “business within the business”. Customer feedback from your portfolio will directly inform our product roadmap and operating model. You’ll operate with the judgment of an owner, not just execute a playbook.

What You'll Own

Commercial strategy

  • Own a portfolio of strategic biopharma accounts; drive the full commercial lifecycle - from implementation and onboarding through to retention and partnership expansion

  • Develop and execute account-level strategy, identifying expansion opportunities and leading renewal negotiations to achieve industry-leading retention rates

  • Monitor usage patterns, engagement signals, and business outcomes to proactively grow accounts and manage partnership signals

  • Transform satisfied customers into vocal advocates who provide references, case studies, testimonials, and speak at industry events

  • Serve as the voice of the customer to Product, Engineering, Sales, and Scientific teams, ensuring market feedback drives our product roadmap and strategic priorities

Lead Implementation and Drive Adoption

  • Orchestrate complex customer implementations including platform configuration, custom development, and data integrations aligned to customer use cases

  • Design and execute account-specific onboarding strategies, facilitating executive workshops, design sessions, and hands-on trainings that accelerate time-to-value

  • Proactively communicate product updates, new capabilities, and innovative use cases to maximize customer value realization

Provide Expert Technical Support

  • Diagnose and resolve platform issues through systematic troubleshooting, documenting problems clearly and coordinating with Engineering on appropriate resolution paths

  • Develop deep platform expertise that enables you to answer complex technical questions and guide customers through sophisticated workflows

  • Create feedback loops that ensure technical issues inform long-term product improvements

Who You Are

Essential Qualifications

  • 8+ years of customer success, management consulting, partnerships, account management, or implementation experience in pharmaceutical, biopharma, biotech, or life sciences industries

  • Working knowledge of drug development processes, portfolio management, and deal evaluation frameworks

  • Demonstrated ability to navigate complex, multi-stakeholder decision-making within large enterprise organizations

  • Strong technical aptitude, with the ability to quickly master sophisticated software platforms and translate technical capabilities into business value

  • Exceptional executive communication skills

  • Entrepreneurial mindset with comfort operating in fast-paced, high-growth environments where priorities evolve quickly

 

Bonus points

  • Direct experience in biopharma Search & Evaluation, Business Development, Licensing, Portfolio Management, or Strategy roles

  • Track record of driving measurable customer outcomes, achieving retention and expansion targets

  • Hands-on experience with AI/ML platforms, advanced analytics tools, or decision intelligence software

  • Proficiency with customer success platforms (HubSpot, etc.)

  • Advanced degree (MS, PhD, MBA) in life sciences, business, or a related field

jobs.title: Prevention Analyst - Pentesting
jobs.description:
Prevention Analyst - Pentesting

About this role


We are looking for a Prevention Analyst - Pentester, to join our Prevention track. An attacker does not look at one server in isolation. They look at everything a company exposes to the internet and work out where to start. You will do the same for our clients, taking the attacker’s view of their external attack surface, seeing what an attacker sees, and doing what an attacker would do next.

That means reading the story behind an attack surface. A forgotten subdomain, an old login portal, and a misconfigured mail server may each look minor on their own. Together they can show how an organisation has grown, where its blind spots are, and where someone could get in. When you find a potential weak point, you dig into it technically to find out how far an attacker could actually go.

This is not a classic penetration testing role. The deep dive draws on pentest methodology and expertise, but it is not a full pentest, and you will not spend your weeks writing long reports. We focus on finding the high impact vulnerabilities that need attention now and getting them to the client in a form they can act on.

This is for someone with hands on pentesting experience who wants to work across many customer environments, sharpen their attacker mindset, and grow into owning complex prevention engagements end to end.

What you will do

  • Assess clients’ external attack surface as a whole, from the attacker’s perspective.

  • Identify gaps and weaknesses across the surface, not just within a single asset, and work out how they connect.

  • Run technical deep dives into potential weak points to establish how far an attacker could get in practice.

  • Separate what needs fixing now from what does not, and focus on high and critical findings with immediate impact.

  • Turn technical findings into short, clear advice that clients can understand and act on.

  • Share what you learn with the team and actively pick up what others know. We work on problems together.

  • Contribute to improving our approach, sharing ideas that make assessments faster, clearer, and more useful for clients.

What you will need

  • Hands on penetration testing experience and a solid grasp of pentest methodology, particularly for external infrastructure and web applications.

  • The ability to think like an attacker, to look at a set of exposed assets and see where you would start and why.

  • Good judgement about real world impact, so you can tell an interesting finding from an urgent one.

  • The ability to explain technical findings to non technical readers, briefly and without losing accuracy.

  • A collaborative way of working and a genuine interest in learning and growing with colleagues, not working as a solo player.

  • Comfortable working across multiple client environments in parallel.

  • Fluent English.

Nice-to-have

  • Certifications such as OSCP, BSCP, or CPTS.

  • A proven bug bounty track record or other real world offensive security experience.

  • Experience working with SMEs or mid market customers on security topics.

What we offer

  • A meaningful mission, protecting organisations across Europe from real world cyber threats.

  • Work with top tier professionals from national CERTs, intelligence agencies, and leading tech backgrounds.

  • A remote friendly culture with quarterly meetups and annual company retreats, for example in Spain, Portugal, or Italy.

  • Thursday socials to stay connected.

  • A generous time off policy, including wellbeing and volunteering days.

About Eye Security


Eye Security is providing cybersecurity with embedded cyber insurance solutions for organisations across Europe. Headquartered in the Netherlands, we are already over 190 FTEs and continue to grow internationally, having secured our Series C funding of 60 million.

We combine cutting edge technology with hands on expertise to detect, respond to, and recover from cyber threats in real time. Our team brings together talent from intelligence, military, tech, and consulting backgrounds, all united by a shared mission, to make enterprise grade cybersecurity accessible to every business, not just the big players.

At Eye, you will work on projects with an international footprint, solving real world challenges and helping to build a safer digital future for our clients.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer in Test II, NavNative
jobs.description:
Mapbox is the leading real-time location platform for a new generation of location-aware businesses. Mapbox is the only platform that equips organizations with the full set of tools to power the navigation of people, packages, and vehicles everywhere. More than 4 million registered developers have chosen Mapbox because of the platform’s flexibility, security and privacy compliance. Organizations use Mapbox applications, data, SDKs and APIs to create customized and immersive experiences that delight their customers. 

What We Do

The Navigation Native team builds the high-performance C++ engine that serves as the "brain" of our Navigation SDKs. This library runs directly on end-user systems (on-board), powering everything from mobile apps to in-vehicle infotainment systems for partners like BMW, Porsche, and Zeekr.

We solve the fundamental challenges of movement: transforming noisy GPS/IMU data into precise map-matching, managing complex road-network graphs, supporting routes and alternatives, tracking progress along a route, and providing "Electronic Horizon" capabilities for ADAS. Our work happens at the edge, supporting location frequencies up to 10Hz and ensuring a seamless experience even in tunnels or dense urban canyons.

As AI becomes embedded in modern engineering workflows, we value engineers who can thoughtfully integrate AI into design, development, and decision-making. Our interview process will include discussion of how you use AI in your engineering workflow.

What You'll Do

We are looking for smart, fast-learning engineers who care as much about proving that navigation works as about making it work. As an SDE(T), you will:

  • Build and maintain the unit, integration, and functional test architecture for a C++17 library, and the CMake and CI pipelines that run it.

  • Turn real-world location recordings into regression tests, and define the quality metrics for map-matching, routing, and route-following.

  • Keep the quality signal fast and trustworthy: eliminate flaky tests, run sanitizer and performance builds, and track coverage.

  • Build AI-driven test tooling: agent-based test generation, automated dogfooding and triage, and AI-assisted PR review.

  • Partner with feature engineers on testability and review designs for how they will be verified.

  • Thoughtfully leverage AI tools in your workflow and set the standard for how the team uses them. 

What We Believe Are Important Traits for This Role

  •  5+ years of experience in C++17: comfortable writing test code and tooling, reading production code, and debugging with sanitizers and profilers. Python or similar for harnesses and analysis.

  • Proven experience building test infrastructure for a large native codebase: test frameworks, CMake, and CI systems.

  • A data-driven mindset: you define metrics, build the tooling to measure them, and use them to argue for or against a change.

  • Experience diagnosing hard-to-reproduce failures: flakiness, platform-specific behavior, memory and threading bugs.

  • Strong English skills, with the ability to explain test results, risk, and trade-offs to peers and stakeholders.

Would be a Plus

  • Familiarity with navigation concepts (map matching, dead reckoning, route progress, or Electronic Horizon).

  • Experience with replay- or simulation-based testing using real sensor and GPS data.

  • Hands-on experience building AI- or agent-based developer tooling for testing, code review, or triage.

  • Experience with coverage tooling, performance benchmarking, or testing SDKs through generated bindings.


Employment Requirements

  • Employment Type: Full-time

jobs.description:
About Alta Ares


Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

About the Role
We are building next-generation interceptor drones and are looking for a Senior Jet Engine Design Engineer to lead the development of small-scale jet propulsion systems (12–25 kg thrust class), from concept to flight-ready hardware. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role in a fast-moving startup environment where speed and iteration matter more than lengthy upfront studies.

Responsibilities:

  • Design and develop new small jet engines (12–25 kg thrust range) in-house, optimized for very low production cost

  • Own the aerodynamic design of turbine components, balancing performance, manufacturability, and cost

  • Design a large portion of the turbine for metal 3D printing (additive manufacturing), leveraging design-for-AM principles to reduce part count, weight, and cost

  • Work closely with 3D printing operations to define printable geometries, tolerances, post-processing, and qualify parts for flight use

  • Drive a rapid, fail-fast iteration process: build, test, learn, and redesign quickly rather than relying on long analytical phases before prototyping

  • Integrate propulsion systems into airframes such as flying wings and other interceptor drone configurations, working with aerostructures and systems teams

  • Apply and enforce design rules for operation in extreme environments (cold and hot climates, rain, humidity, icing conditions) to ensure engine reliability across the full operational envelope

  • Contribute to engine testing (bench and flight), performance validation, and continuous design improvement

Candidate Profile:

  • Minimum 8 years of experience in jet engine / gas turbine design, with a proven track record of having designed and delivered engine models (not just component-level work)

  • Strong hands-on experience with small jet engines in the 12–25 kg thrust class

  • Solid global understanding of jet engine architecture: compressor, combustor, turbine, fuel system, controls, and their interactions

  • Experience designing turbine/engine components for metal additive manufacturing (DfAM), and practical knowledge of metal 3D printing processes and constraints

  • Comfortable working in a rapid-iteration, fail-fast development culture rather than a traditional long-cycle aerospace process

  • Experience integrating propulsion systems into airframes (flying wing or similar unconventional platforms is a strong plus)

  • Knowledge of design requirements for extreme operating environments (temperature extremes, precipitation, icing)

  • Ability to work autonomously in a small, fast-paced startup team, wearing multiple hats when needed

Nice to Have

  • Experience with UAV/drone propulsion specifically (vs. manned aviation)

  • Familiarity with low-cost manufacturing strategies for defense/dual-use hardware

  • Prior startup or skunkworks experience

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

 

As a Senior AI Deployment Strategist, you will bridge the gap between vision and execution, ensuring our customers not only see the potential of AI but realize its value in their operations. This role is a unique blend of strategic advisory and hands-on deployment leadership, spanning both presales and postsales phases. You will act as a trusted advisor to C-suite executives, architecting AI solutions that drive transformation and delivering measurable business outcomes.

 

You will be embedded in our most strategic accounts, diagnosing business challenges, designing AI-powered solutions, and leading their deployment from concept to full-scale adoption. This role demands a rare combination of executive presence, technical credibility, and commercial acumen, with a focus on both winning and delivering high-impact AI initiatives.

 

What You Will Do

 

Strategic Advisory & C-Suite Partnership

• Serve as the lead strategic advisor for a portfolio of high-value enterprise clients, building trusted relationships with executive leadership (CEO, CTO, CIO).

• Lead C-suite workshops to diagnose business drivers and co-create multi-year AI transformation roadmaps aligned with corporate strategy.

• Develop and present compelling business cases and proposals, articulating the ROI of AI adoption and the value of Mistral’s platform.

 

Presales: Shaping the Vision

• Partner with sales and product teams to identify and qualify opportunities, positioning Mistral’s solutions as the catalyst for enterprise transformation.

• Design tailored AI strategies and proof-of-concepts that address critical business challenges and demonstrate tangible value.

• Act as a subject matter expert in client engagements, ensuring our solutions are understood, trusted, and adopted.

 

Postsales: Driving Deployment & Adoption

• Own the end-to-end success of AI deployments, from strategic planning to operational integration, ensuring solutions are embedded into the customer’s core workflows.

• Lead cross-functional teams of engineers, data scientists, and product managers to execute deployment roadmaps and deliver measurable results.

• Navigate organizational complexity and drive change management to ensure seamless adoption and long-term success.

 

Commercial Growth & Thought Leadership

• Identify and cultivate expansion opportunities within accounts, connecting Mistral’s capabilities to new business challenges and driving commercial growth.

• Mentor junior strategists and contribute to the development of best practices, methodologies, and playbooks for customer engagement.

• Represent Mistral AI as a thought leader through speaking engagements, executive briefings, and industry contributions.

 
 

What We're Looking For

 

• You have 8+ years of experience in technical management consulting, enterprise technology, or a customer-facing strategic role, with a focus on AI/ML, data architecture, or digital transformation.

• You hold a degree in a relevant scientific field (e.g., Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, etc.)

• You possess a deep, practical expertise in AI/ML concepts, enterprise data architecture, and modern software development with hands-on development of AI solutions—enough to credibly engage with technical teams and executives alike.

• You have a proven track record of engaging and influencing C-suite executives, with the ability to navigate complex conversations and align AI strategies with business objectives.

• You excel at structuring ambiguous problems into actionable programs and thrive in fast-paced, high-stakes environments.

• You are equally comfortable in presales and postsales: shaping deals, designing solutions, and ensuring their successful deployment.

• You have experience managing high-value accounts, understanding deal mechanics, and building compelling cases for investment.

• You are a collaborative leader who can motivate cross-functional teams and drive results through influence, not authority.

 

We are looking for adaptable, low-ego team players who are passionate about turning AI vision into reality and delivering transformative impact for our customers.

Mistral is hiring a Head of FDE Learning Programs to build the learning system for one of the company’s fastest-growing organizations. Your mandate is to make capability grow as fast as headcount without lowering the bar for customer work.

You will own:

  • Learning content: Build practical learning across three areas: technical skills, strategic and business capabilities, and product enablement.

  • Onboarding: Build a clear path from a new hire’s first week to independent customer work.

  • Technical bootcamps: Turn new products, research, and field methods into practical training for customer work.

  • We care about people and outputs.

  • Bureaucracy is where urgency goes to vanish. You talk to whoever you need to talk to. The best idea wins, whether it comes from a principal engineer or someone in their first week.

  • Always ask why. The best solutions come from deep understanding, not from copying what worked before

  • We say what we mean. Feedback is direct, timely, and given because we care.

  • No politics. Low ego, high standards.

  • We embrace an unstructured environment and find joy in it.

About you

You have helped build a learning, enablement, or capability function for a technical organization during rapid growth. You can start as the first dedicated owner, deliver useful programs immediately, and build the team and operating model needed to serve several hundred people.

  • You are technically fluent enough to work credibly with AI engineers, Product, and Science, inspect the substance of a program, and challenge material that is unclear or outdated.

  • You have designed programs that work across cohorts, regions, and experience levels without reducing the content to generic training.

  • You can lead work across senior stakeholders, subject-matter experts, managers, and operational partners without relying on reporting lines.

  • You can make firm trade-offs when hiring demand, expert capacity, and program quality compete for attention.

  • You pay attention to the full learner experience, including communications, scheduling, practice, feedback, and manager follow-through.

  • You use evidence to decide which programs to expand, revise, or stop.

  • You communicate clearly with executives, managers, technical experts, and learners.

  • You are fluent in English and can work with teams across regions and time zones.

Ideally, you have

  • Scaled a one-person or small learning function into a team and program that served hundreds of technical employees.

  • Built onboarding that kept pace with rapid hiring in an engineering, FDE, solutions, consulting, or professional-services organization.

  • Designed and operated technical bootcamps or other cohort-based learning programs.

  • Worked in technical DevRel, developer education, or a related role built around demos, code examples, workshops, and practitioner communities.

  • Built role- and level-based curricula connected to skills frameworks or career progression.

  • Managed a global program with contributors and learners across multiple regions.

  • Worked closely with Product, Engineering, Science, People, and customer-facing teams.

  • Designed practical assessments, readiness standards, or certification where appropriate.

  • Used learning platforms, knowledge systems, AI coaches, or program-operations tooling.

  • Worked in AI/ML or another technically complex and fast-changing field.

Why this role matters

Mistral is compressing years of organization growth into two. An FDE organization of several hundred people cannot depend on manager-by-manager onboarding, one-off sessions, and informal access to experts. If learning capacity trails hiring, ramp times would lengthen, standards would diverge, and teams would repeat the same mistakes across regions.

This role will build the programs, teaching network, and systems at the same pace as the organization. Two years from now, success would mean several hundred Deployment Strategists and Applied AI Engineers working from shared standards, learning new capabilities quickly, and improving the system with evidence from customer work.

jobs.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all.

We run it all on our own metal, our own network, our own datacenters — which means when something breaks, the fix is ours to write.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it.

The Role

Agents don't run in browsers. They run in sandboxes — and you will lead the team building ours.

You will manage the team — hiring, coaching, performance, growth paths, honest feedback — while staying close to the code: roughly half your time in architecture decisions and the hardest technical problems the team faces, the other half leading your squad.

We build secure, isolated, network-controlled environments with snapshotting primitives, designed for AI agents and reinforcement-learning workloads. An RL training run doesn't need one environment; it needs thousands, created and destroyed every second. An agent needs to be sandboxed from the world while still feeling fast enough to be useful. That tension — airtight isolation, at fleet scale, at low latency — is the product.

Your customers are the people building the next generation of AI software on our infrastructure; the primitives you ship become the runtime their agents live in.

What You Will Do

  • Build the isolation layer: microVMs or containers, namespaces, cgroups, seccomp, snapshot and restore.

  • Own the security boundary. Customers run code they didn't write and can't fully trust — your systems make that safe.

  • Scale to fleets: creation latency, density, and lifecycle management for thousands of concurrent environments.

  • Design and build alongside your team, owning the architecture and the hardest implementation decisions.

  • Grow the engineers, not just the software — set the standard for ownership and coach people past their comfort zone.

  • Own people management for the team: hiring, performance, growth paths, and honest feedback.

  • Partner with Product Managers to turn frontier research needs into shippable primitives.

What We're Looking For

  • 3+ years of real people leadership. You have managed engineers — hired, coached, given honest feedback, and grown them. Hands-on contribution matters here, but this role is judged on the team you build and lead, not just the code you write.

  • Deep Linux internals: namespaces, cgroups, seccomp, virtualization — ideally microVMs of the Firecracker class.

  • You have shipped production systems in Go. Not dabbled. Shipped.

  • You understand network isolation at the packet level — not just firewall rules.

  • Performance instincts: you know what a syscall costs, and you have the profiles to prove you've cared.

  • 8+ years building backend or infrastructure systems.

  • You have partnered with product, design, and business teams to ship software that reached real users.

  • A low-ego, team-first mindset. We care less about your exact domain and more about whether you are the kind of technical force other engineers want to work alongside.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

As a Defense Success Manager, you own what happens to our most strategic defense and sovereign accounts after the build: you make deployed AI stick in real workflows — often in restricted or disconnected environments — keep production commitments healthy, defend renewals, and source the expansion signals that Sales closes.

Mistral's Solutions teams (Deployment Strategists and Forward Deployed Engineers) co-create high-value AI use cases with customers in these environments. Your job is to make those investments successful beyond delivery — adopting what has been built, operating it with confidence, demonstrating its impact, and scaling value across the institution. You will work with mission owners, program stakeholders, end users, security and IT teams, and across Mistral with Solutions, Product, Engineering and Support.

This is not a high-volume, ticket-queue customer success role. Portfolios are small and deep — typically one or two flagship accounts plus a small number of adjacent programs. It calls for a strategic account mindset, the technical judgment to navigate complex and constrained deployment environments, and the energy to build the customer success function as Mistral grows. Travel to customer sites, including secure facilities, is a regular part of the job.

You will join on one of two tracks (and can move between them):

  • Adoption track — embedded in flagship programs while Solutions is still delivering. You own the adoption and change-management motion around the build: user waves, enablement, champions, training programs, and the evidence that proves value is landing.

  • Operational track — you take accounts through a structured handover once Solutions completes delivery, and own the run phase end-to-end: operational health, value realization, renewals, and expansion signals.

In both tracks you operate in close partnership with Solutions: they deliver and hand over; you own post-handover; they re-engage on expansion signals. Occasionally, account teams will also pull you into late-stage pre-sales — authoring the customer training and scale-up plan that gives a buyer confidence in the rollout.


What You Will Do


Own the customer success and value plan

  • Build a clear view of each account's objectives, stakeholders, deployed use cases, commitments and risks. Translate it into a shared success plan with owners, milestones and measurable outcomes.

  • Establish a practical operating cadence with customer sponsors, business owners, IT and delivery teams. Lead success reviews that make progress, risks, decisions and next steps clear.

  • Define a baseline and track the outcomes that matter for each use case: adoption and usage against entitled seats, customer satisfaction, operational health and business impact. Turn the evidence into a clear value narrative.

Make deployment realities part of the success plan

  • Understand how each customer's deployment model — on-premises, VPC or serverless — affects the products and use cases they can access, operate and scale. Validate the specifics with the technical teams rather than assuming feature parity or identical operating models.

  • Identify the practical implications of deployment choices: security and data requirements, access and integrations, release and upgrade cadence, available features, capacity, observability and support processes. Explain the trade-offs clearly to customer and Mistral stakeholders.

  • Translate those constraints into an actionable adoption plan: align enablement and release communications with the version the customer actually runs, account for security approvals and upgrade windows, and agree how to measure usage when telemetry is limited.

  • Spot risks early, qualify their impact on adoption, renewal or value, and coordinate the right Solutions, Product, Engineering or Support owners to resolve them. Set clear expectations without making unvalidated technical or roadmap commitments.

Drive adoption, autonomy and sustained value

  • Help customer teams move from a delivered use case to regular, effective use. Identify the users, workflows and change-management needs that determine whether it sticks.

  • Coordinate onboarding, training, product updates and hands-on enablement with the right Mistral and customer teams. Develop customer champions and train-the-trainer motions so adoption scales beyond direct Mistral involvement.

  • Prepare the transition from delivery to run: clarify operational ownership, support and escalation paths, and the resources users need to succeed independently.

  • Monitor adoption and customer health, investigate where usage or value is falling short, and lead a coordinated plan to address the causes.

Defend and grow the commercial relationship

  • Own the renewal motion for your accounts: know every renewal date, the auto vs non-auto renewal terms, and the risk story behind each one. Run the renewal play early — no surprises at renewal time.

  • Track and improve account NRR. Identify new use cases, teams and expansion opportunities, and share them with the account team grounded in demonstrated value.

  • Lead business reviews with the account team: value delivered, risks owned, decisions needed, roadmap asks.

Bring the customer voice into Mistral

  • Gather and qualify feedback from users, technical teams and sponsors. Distinguish enablement needs from product gaps, deployment constraints and support issues, and route each to the right owner.

  • Track important requests and communicate progress and limitations back to the customer, while Product and Engineering retain ownership of product and technical decisions.

Build the company as well as the account

  • Create the playbooks, success plans, handover practices and measurement approaches that are missing. Test them with customers, improve them, and make them reusable across accounts.

  • Bring structure to ambiguity: identify what needs to happen, make a plan, mobilize the right people and follow through — without waiting for a perfect process or detailed instructions.

  • Roughly a fifth of your time is protected, rotating build time for exactly this work; it is part of the job, not extra to it.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience owning outcomes for enterprise or institutional customers of technical products or deployed solutions — adoption and commercial outcomes (retention, renewal, expansion), not relationship management or activity reporting.

  • Strong technical fluency in secure enterprise deployment models. You can identify what a deployment type (on-premise, disconnected, air-gapped) means for available features, telemetry, upgrades and accreditation, and you validate specifics with technical teams instead of assuming parity.

  • Ability to engage credibly with architects, engineers, IT and security stakeholders, while translating technical trade-offs into clear implications for mission owners and executives. You know when to bring in a deeper technical expert.

  • Comfort operating under security, compliance and confidentiality constraints, including restricted or classified environments and strict information-handling rules.

  • Strong ownership and builder energy. You have created structure or improved a process in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment and are motivated to build a company, not wait for clear directions.

  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management and execution skills. You align teams without formal authority, surface risks early and drive decisions through to completion

  • Analytical and commercially minded: you can define meaningful success metrics with imperfect data, assess customer health, and are comfortable carrying renewal and NRR accountability.


Nice to have

  • Experience serving defense, public sector or critical infrastructure customers, including sovereign or classified programs.

  • Experience with AI, machine learning, data platforms or complex enterprise software, including production deployments in regulated or security-sensitive environments.

  • Experience working alongside deployment, engineering or professional services teams on custom use cases, and the transition from implementation to ongoing operation.

  • Familiarity with public procurement, framework agreements and multi-year option structures.

Security & Compliance criteria

  • Eligibility: must hold citizenship in the target territory (France for now).

  • Clearable: must meet all local requirements for high-level security clearance (e.g. no criminal record, fulfillment of national service obligations).

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Analytics first: Du baust CRM und Lifecycle Marketing bei Foodji komplett neu auf, vom analytischen Fundament bis zur Integration der Systeme – datengetrieben, KI-enabled und mit hohem Iterationstempo.

In dieser neu geschaffenen Rolle verantwortest du die Segmentierungs- und Journey-Logik unserer B2C-Kommunikation. Dein Werkzeug sind Daten, nicht Pixel: Du entwickelst Hypothesen, übersetzt sie in Events, Segmente und Journey-Konzepte, wertest Tests aus und iterierst schnell auf Basis der Ergebnisse. Kampagnen und Content kommen aus dem Marketing- und UI/UX-Team, du lieferst das Wer, Wann und Warum. Rund 60 bis 70 Prozent deiner Arbeit sind Analytics, und KI-Tools wie Claude nutzt du dabei ganz selbstverständlich.

Foodji ist dabei kein klassischer Onlineshop: Jeder Foodji hat individuelle Stocklevels und Produktkombinationen. Genau das macht CRM bei uns besonders spannend. Dazu kommt eine riesige Datenbasis: Fast alle Kund:innen sind registriert und haben ein eigenes Profil. Du entwickelst die Logik für dynamische, hochgradig segmentierte Kommunikation über alle Kanäle – von der Foodji App über In-App-Messages, Push und Mail bis zum Foodji Screen direkt am Gerät – und nutzt Daten, um sie kontinuierlich weiterzuentwickeln.

Deine Mission bei Foodji

  • Du legst das analytische und konzeptionelle Fundament für eine skalierbare CRM- und Lifecycle-Funktion für unsere B2C-Kund:innen.

  • Von der Hypothese über Segmentierung und Testdesign bis zur Auswertung von A/B-Tests und Kohorten: Du definierst, was wir ausprobieren, misst, was wirkt, und iterierst schnell auf Basis der Ergebnisse.

  • Welche Events lösen welche Kommunikation aus? Du definierst sie auf Basis unserer Daten, konzipierst dynamische Segmente und Journeys, die Stocklevels, Produktkombinationen und Nutzerbedürfnisse berücksichtigen, und entscheidest datenbasiert, ob App, In-App, Push, Mail oder Foodji Screen der richtige Kanal ist.

  • In Snowflake und mit KI-Tools wie Claude analysierst du Daten eigenständig, findest die relevanten Hebel und priorisierst Maßnahmen nach ihrem erwarteten Impact.

  • Mit Marketing, Product, Revenue Management und BI arbeitest du eng zusammen und machst Daten und technische Möglichkeiten für CRM nutzbar. Dem Team, das Kampagnen und Content umsetzt, lieferst du Segmente, Journey-Konzepte und klare Briefings.

  • Du verantwortest Datenqualität und Governance deiner Segmente, Events und Systeme und stellst sicher, dass alles performant, sicher und datenschutzkonform läuft.

jobs.title: Senior Growth Product Manager
jobs.description:
Data quality is the bottleneck of the AI era. Every Fortune 500 is trying to solve it. We're the team they call.

Soda is the data quality layer for Disney, Ralph Lauren, CBRE, HelloFresh, 2K Games, and Nubank. Our open-source engine, Soda Core, is used by companies like Tesla, Slack, Adyen, Walmart, and JPMC. The category is growing fast because AI doesn't work on bad data, and we're hiring a Senior Growth Product Manager to get customers using Soda faster and on more of their data.

About Us

Soda's mission is to monitor the world's decisions. We're building the first Data & AI performance monitoring platform that spans data collection to automated decision-making. Soda helps customers find, understand, and fix data quality issues by combining automated post-production monitoring with pre-production pipeline data testing.

Soda was founded in 2019 by Maarten (employee #5 at Collibra) and Tom (creator of multiple open-source projects generating hundreds of millions in value). We commercialize through Soda Cloud and we're well-funded, with investors like Point 9 Capital, Hummingbird, Singular, and Eurazeo.

The Role

You'll lead our adoption team, a small group of frontend, full-stack, and AI engineers. The team works on onboarding and activation, on keeping workflows coherent across the product, on customer-facing dashboards, and on AI features that save users work.

Most of our roadmap is driven by what customers and prospects ask for. This team's work is driven by adoption metrics, because customers rarely ask for the things that would make them use Soda more. You'll start from a hypothesis, for example that changing a flow will get 20% more data contracts created, ship the change, and check whether it worked.

We sell to enterprises, so sample sizes are small and A/B tests rarely reach significance. You'll use product analytics, session replays, and conversations with users, and you'll often have to decide with incomplete data. This is a product role. If most of your growth experience is in paid acquisition or lifecycle email, it's probably the wrong fit. You'll also work closely with our Growth team, which is led by a co-founder, on launches and messaging.

What You'll Do

  • Own the adoption metrics for Soda Cloud: time to first verified contract for new accounts, data coverage (datasets with contracts and monitors), weekly active datasets and users, and usage of AI features. You'll define them, make sure we can measure them, and improve them.
  • Own the UX of workflows across the product and keep them coherent for our two kinds of users: data engineers, and business users such as data stewards and governance leads.
  • Find where customers get stuck between signing the contract and running Soda on most of their data, and decide what to fix first.
  • Design and ship onboarding flows that get a new team to first value within days, including self-serve paths for technical teams that want to evaluate Soda on their own.
  • Put AI to work on adoption: decide which steps an agent should do for the user, ship them with the team, and measure whether people keep using them.
  • Work with Growth on launches and product marketing, and with our customer engineers on whatever is blocking rollouts at customers.

Hiring Process

  1. Application: your CV, plus a short answer about one metric you moved (what it was, what you shipped, what happened, and what didn't work)
  2. 15-minute phone screen
  3. First interview (60 min): a deep dive into product growth work you've done. Part of it is showing us something you shipped that you'd still be proud to demo.
  4. Second interview (60 min): a working session on a real Soda adoption problem
  5. Culture fit (45 min)

We answer every application, and every candidate hears back within 3–5 days of each step. If it's not a hell yes, it's a no, and we'll tell you quickly and kindly.

Requirements

You Should Have

  • 5+ years in product, including at least 2 owning growth, activation, onboarding, or adoption in B2B SaaS: you were accountable for a metric for long enough to see whether your changes worked. In your application, tell us which metric it was, where it started and where it ended, what you shipped, and what didn't work.
  • Product craft and taste: you love software and have used a lot of it yourself, so you know what a good product feels like. You keep scope small, work in short cycles with engineers and designers, run your own customer calls, and have well-reasoned opinions about UX.
  • An AI-native way of working and building: you've shipped an AI-powered feature and measured whether people use it, you prototype with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.), and you're happy to open a small PR yourself for something like a copy change.
  • You do your own analysis: you write SQL, build funnels yourself, and know when a sample is too small to conclude anything.
  • Experience with technical products: you've built for engineers or data teams and are comfortable talking about pipelines, warehouses, and APIs.
  • Clear writing and comfort working async: we're a distributed team across 12+ countries, and most decisions happen in writing, in English.

The five years don't all have to be in a PM role. If you were a product engineer or a founder and owned a growth metric, please apply.

Good to Have

  • Data quality, data observability, data governance, or data infrastructure experience.
  • Experience with product-led growth at a company that also sells to enterprises.
  • Experience with Shape Up or another fixed-time, variable-scope way of working.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Compensation €120,000–140,000/year + equity.
  • Outside Belgium, this is a contractor position.
  • Fully remote (EU-based), with a Belgian office available if you want one.
  • In-person kickoffs every two months in cool locations across Europe, three days with the whole product and engineering team.
  • All the tokens you need, across all frontier models.
  • Real ownership, real impact, no micromanagement.
  • A senior team that ships, across 12+ countries.

Our Values

We value freedom with responsibility, transparency, and a growth mindset. We avoid politics, have no tolerance for dishonesty, and value open and direct communication without judgment. We proactively bring up and address potential issues before they become critical, and we overcommunicate frequently. Working at Soda, you will have full autonomy to make impactful product and roadmap decisions.

❤️ Why you will love to join Soda

  • You own the adoption metrics: you decide how we measure adoption and what we do to improve it.
  • Lots of room to improve: we already have enterprise customers and usage data, and we've done very little growth work so far.
  • Your own engineering team: you'll work with dedicated engineers who build agentically, so your ideas get shipped quickly.
  • Be part of a transformation: data quality is having its moment, and we're at the front of it.
  • Work on your own terms: fully remote, flexible hours, colleagues in 12+ countries.

😡 What you might not love

  • Rapidly changing priorities: our roadmap can pivot quickly. It's a fast-paced environment with a LOT of work to be done.
  • Small numbers: we have relatively few accounts and feedback is slow. If you're used to deciding from consumer-scale data, you may find that frustrating.
  • No playbook: this is the first dedicated growth PM role at Soda.

Diese Position richtet sich an eine Person, die eigenverantwortlich arbeitet, Prozesse aktiv mitgestaltet und gemeinsam mit Homaris langfristig wachsen möchte.

What You'll Do

Kreditkartenabrechnungen bearbeiten. Du bearbeitest und buchst die Kreditkartenabrechnungen über Pleo.

Prozesse digital weiterentwickeln. Du optimierst proaktiv Prozesse und erhöhst dabei den Digitalisierungsgrad.

What Makes You a Fit

Relevante Ausbildung und Erfahrung. Du hast eine abgeschlossene kaufmännische Ausbildung und mindestens drei Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Buchhaltung.

Kenntnisse im deutschen Rechnungswesen. Du verfügst über Kenntnisse des HGB und des Umsatzsteuergesetzes.

DATEV-Erfahrung. Du bringst Erfahrung mit der Buchhaltungssoftware DATEV mit.

The Environment

Homaris ist konsequent langfristig ausgerichtet. Wir investieren nicht in kurzfristiges Wachstum mit dem Ziel, schnell zu verkaufen. Wir bauen etwas Nachhaltiges und Substanzielles auf – und suchen Menschen, die diesen Weg gemeinsam mit uns gehen und langfristig Verantwortung übernehmen wollen.

jobs.title: Kundenberater / Kundenbetreuer (m/w/d) – Service mit Persönlichkeit
jobs.description:
Du liebst persönlichen Kundenkontakt. Bei uns verbindest du ihn mit internationalen Aufgaben und der Chance, beruflich weiterzukommen.

Wir sind Akademis, eine mehrfach ausgezeichnete Bildungsberatung. Wir helfen Familien, das passende Internat im Ausland für ihr Kind zu finden, und begleiten sie bei den nächsten Schritten. Für unser neues Büro in Berlin-Frohnau suchen wir jemanden, der gerne telefoniert, aufmerksam zuhört und Freude daran hat, sich persönlich um Menschen zu kümmern.

Unsere Familien vertrauen uns eine wichtige Entscheidung an. Sie schätzen eine Ansprechperson, die ihre Wünsche kennt, verständlich erklärt und zuverlässig nachfasst. Genau das lieben wir an unserer Arbeit: wenn aus einem ersten Gespräch eine vertraute Zusammenarbeit wird und Eltern wissen, dass sie sich auf uns verlassen können.

Vielleicht arbeitest du bisher in der Hotellerie, in der Gästebetreuung oder im Kundenservice und möchtest deine Erfahrung in einem neuen Umfeld einsetzen. Bei uns bist du als Quereinsteiger herzlich willkommen. Noch wichtiger als ein perfekter Lebenslauf sind uns deine Persönlichkeit, deine Verlässlichkeit und deine Freude daran, Familien und junge Menschen zu begleiten.

Du möchtest dich einbringen und beruflich weiterkommen? Wir arbeiten dich persönlich ein und unterstützen dich dabei, deine eigenen Familien zunehmend selbstständig zu betreuen. In unserem kleinen Team kannst du Abläufe mitgestalten und mehr Verantwortung übernehmen. Mit deiner fachlichen Entwicklung und guten Leistungen soll sich auch dein Gehalt weiterentwickeln

Aufgaben

Familien beraten und von Anfang bis Ende begleiten: Du lernst Eltern und Jugendliche kennen, berätst Interessierte zu unserem Angebot und betreust deine Familien während der Vorbereitung und des Internatsaufenthalts bis zur Rückkehr. Du hörst aufmerksam zu, gehst auf individuelle Wünsche ein und hältst von dir aus Kontakt – telefonisch und per E-Mail.

Bewerbungen, Schulbesuche und Termine organisieren: Du koordinierst Bewerbungsunterlagen, Schulbesuche und die Vorbereitung auf Aufnahmeverfahren. Du pflegst Kundendaten sorgfältig, behältst Fristen im Blick und fasst selbstständig nach, wenn Unterlagen oder Rückmeldungen fehlen. Deine Familien wissen, welche Schritte als Nächstes anstehen.

Beziehungen zu internationalen Partnerschulen pflegen: Du kommunizierst auf Englisch mit unseren Partnerschulen, klärst Fragen und stimmst Anforderungen und Abläufe ab. Dabei baust du persönliche Kontakte und eine vertrauensvolle Zusammenarbeit auf.

Eigene Projekte gestalten und umsetzen: Du übernimmst Projekte von der Planung bis zum Abschluss, bringst Ideen ein und verbesserst gemeinsam mit uns Abläufe. Ziele und Zuständigkeiten legen wir zusammen fest.

Profil

Du übernimmst Verantwortung: Du hältst Zusagen ein, bringst Aufgaben nach der Einarbeitung eigenständig zum Abschluss und sprichst Schwierigkeiten frühzeitig an.

Du denkst mit und packst an: Du erkennst, wo dein Beitrag gebraucht wird, unterstützt dein Team und möchtest unser kleines Unternehmen aktiv mitgestalten. Eigene Ideen bringst du ein und hilfst dabei, sie umzusetzen.

Du gehst neue Herausforderungen offen an: Du arbeitest dich engagiert in neue Themen ein, stellst gezielte Fragen und entwickelst deine Fähigkeiten weiter.

Du verbindest Sorgfalt mit Tempo: Du arbeitest konzentriert und zügig, setzt Prioritäten und behältst parallele Anliegen im Blick. Unterlagen, Daten und Termine prüfst du gewissenhaft auf Richtigkeit und Vollständigkeit. Du hältst Absprachen nachvollziehbar fest und kontrollierst deine Ergebnisse, bevor du sie weitergibst.

Du berätst mit Einfühlungsvermögen: Du telefonierst ausgesprochen gerne, hörst aufmerksam zu und stellst dich auf unterschiedliche Menschen ein. Du nimmst die Wünsche und Sorgen von Eltern und Jugendlichen ernst und kommunizierst auch in anspruchsvollen Situationen herzlich, klar und professionell.

Du arbeitest an Lösungen: Du benennst Probleme klar, überlegst, was du selbst zu ihrer Lösung beitragen kannst, und beziehst rechtzeitig die Unterstützung ein, die du brauchst.

Du bleibst respektvoll und direkt: Du sprichst Meinungsverschiedenheiten sachlich mit den Beteiligten an und trägst auch in anspruchsvollen Situationen zu einer konstruktiven Zusammenarbeit bei.

Du nutzt Feedback zur Weiterentwicklung: Du gehst offen mit eigenen Fehlern und sachlichen Rückmeldungen um, setzt berechtigte Hinweise um und gibst selbst respektvoll Feedback.

Außerdem sprichst und schreibst du sehr gut Deutsch und gut Englisch und gehst sicher mit digitalen Arbeitsmitteln um. Erfahrung in Kundenberatung, Betreuung oder Organisation ist hilfreich. Unsere Partnerschulen und die Besonderheiten der Internatsberatung lernst du während deiner Einarbeitung kennen.

Wir bieten

Persönliche Einarbeitung: Wir begleiten deinen Einstieg. Schritt für Schritt übernimmst du eigene Familien, Aufgaben und Projekte.

Ein wertschätzendes Miteinander: Direkter Austausch, gegenseitige Unterstützung und Raum für Fragen und Ideen gehören zu unserem Arbeitsalltag.

Klare Erwartungen und regelmäßige Rückmeldung: Wir vereinbaren konkrete Ziele für Betreuung, Organisation und Projekte und unterstützen deine Entwicklung.

Gestaltungsspielraum: Du kannst eigene Ideen umsetzen, Abläufe mitentwickeln und mit wachsender Erfahrung weitere Verantwortung übernehmen.

Karriere- und Gehaltsperspektiven: Wir möchten, dass du dich langfristig bei uns weiterentwickelst. Mit wachsender Kompetenz, guten Leistungen und zusätzlicher Verantwortung hast du die Möglichkeit, beruflich voranzukommen und auch dein Gehalt zu steigern. Deine nächsten Entwicklungsschritte besprechen wir gemeinsam.

Fortbildungen und internationale Einblicke: Du baust dein Wissen aus, arbeitest mit internationalen Partnerschulen zusammen und hast die Möglichkeit, an internationalen Branchenveranstaltungen teilzunehmen.

Eine langfristige Festanstellung: Du arbeitest 40 Stunden pro Woche, Montag bis Freitag, an fünf Tagen in unserem Büro in Berlin-Frohnau.
